description: Coastal Erosion - Prince Edward Island is a dataset listed in Open Government portal of Canada, an open data portal, published or maintained by Parks Canada | Parcs Canada. Coastal erosion is the process that removes shoreline material, causing the coastline to retreat inland. The coastal landscape of Prince Edward Island is identified as a region sensitive to sea-level rise. Systematic measurements for coastal erosion were carried out between 2007-2010 using ground surveyed reference transects and shoreline coordinates. Coverage: Canada. The portal files it under the publisher Parks Canada | Parcs Canada. Its tags are Parc national de l’Î.-P.-É., littoral, érosion, changement climatique, processus littoraux. It offers 3 resource(s) in CSV. The portal shows 2024-12-09 as the last update. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is Open Government Licence - Canada (as labelled on the portal). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support natural hazard exposure and risk studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-am-canada-portal.
